themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often changes while you measure it. So the models keep starting by building a small truth set of their own, or by admitting the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization all three models say answers are stochastic and drift faster than any change a brand makes; on identity resolution and B2B buying-group signal they say there is no reliable record of who is really the same person or which accounts were truly in market; on incrementality the platform reacts to the test itself.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, a message, or a buying conversation leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, trained model, or private chat that now holds it. You can estimate whether the rules were honored, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three call ad platforms and agency segments black boxes with no lineage or deletion evidence, and one suggests planting identities to watch what comes back; on B2B signal loss the models say buying groups now talk in private channels that cannot be observed; on incrementality the platforms control both the treatment and the evidence.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every answer on safe agent execution builds a proxy, gateway, or control plane in front of martech writes, with caps on spend, rate, and audience size, and the newest one adds a dry-run diff plus an inventory of which actions can actually be undone; the same move shows up as a single egress checkpoint for consent and a shared pre-send eligibility check for journey orchestration.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the person holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. A shared standard or a central system cannot settle a fight over money, credit, or turf.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models agree agents are paid to look human and propose perks or faster endpoints rather than rules; on the semantic context layer they call conflicting definitions of customer a political settlement, not a modeling gap; on journey orchestration they say channel owners whose bonuses depend on sends will subvert any arbiter that tells them no.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. The models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three build an approved-claims library and then admit that deciding whether wording quietly breaks a claim is a contextual judgment experts themselves dispute; on the semantic context layer they argue for governed plurality instead of one definition; on agent execution one notes prompt injection collapses the line between data and instruction.
